title: Genius Yield | Atlas 2.0: PAB improvements and advanced UTxO features

ms.promise:
Augment Atlas (off-chain transaction building tool by GeniusYield) to support:
・Native Scripts, also known as Simple Scripts and they are elaborated here.
・Plutus Contract Blueprint (CIP-57) which is elaborated here.
ms.criteria:
・With respect to support of Simple Scripts in Atlas, one is able to:
・Specify a native script in Atlas.
・Interact with a native script in Atlas.
・Read (parse) a native script from it's JSON representation in Atlas.
・With respect to support of Plutus Contract Blueprint (CIP-57):
・Atlas is able to read (parse) a generated blueprint file to populate fields of specification, such as datum, redeemer, compiled code etc.
・The populated fields of specification corresponds directly to relevant Atlas types, such as GYDatum, GYRedeemer, etc.
ms.report:
This milestone promised two outputs, summarised below:
・Support of Simple Scripts (also known as Native / Timelock scripts).
・Support of Plutus Contract Blueprint (CIP-57).

We have successfully achieved these outputs. To note that our Atlas framework is open-sourced and code is accessible here.
As evidence, we have prepared video demonstrations showcasing the said functionality and how it achieves the described acceptance criteria.
For output (1), please find it's video here. We also provide a documentation on it, at https://atlas-app.io/additional-features/simple-scripts.
For output (2), here is it's video. And here is it's corresponding documentation: https://atlas-app.io/additional-features/blueprint.
Also, for reference, following modules contain tests for added Simple Script feature:
・GeniusYield.Test.SimpleScript
・GeniusYield.Test.Privnet.SimpleScripts

And tests for added Blueprint feature is in following modules:
・GeniusYield.Test.Blueprint
・GeniusYield.Test.Privnet.Blueprint

The goals of this milestone include:
・Atlas to have it's own coin selection algorithm, as:
・Current algorithm is out-sourced from cardano-wallet repository, available here. We aim to implement a custom variant which would give us greater flexibility and better serve our use-case.
・Own coin selection algorithm also helps us reduce build dependencies, as we would not require dependency upon `cardano-wallet`'s sub-libraries. Less dependency bloat would enable us to more promptly support version updates to GHC (flagship Haskell compiler).
・Current coin selection algorithm is tied deeply with transaction fee estimate cycle, we aim to improve on that so we can reduce from current logarithmic fee estimate iterations to something more constant.

・Improved transaction chaining and parallel transaction building abstractions.
・Improvements to data providers supported by Atlas.

ms.promise:
The goals of this milestone are:
・To make Atlas compile with GHC version 9.10.1 or later.
・It's worth noting that currently, Atlas compiles with GHC version 9.6.5, which lacks some of the features added by GHC 9.10.1 in relevance to JavaScript and WebAssembly backends as a GHC compilation target.
・Exploration and utilisation of Atlas on client side in browsers.
・Currently if one is to make use of Atlas, it is not possible to run it entirely on client side in web browsers but rather one would need to make an API endpoint available from the server backend which the browser client can then call. This is one important difference with off-chain transaction building tools that target JavaScript. GHC 9.10.1 provides useful compilation targets such as WASM & JS with JS FFI interoperability. We aim to make use of these targets and FFI compatibilities to enable Atlas to run entirely on client side.
ms.criteria:
・Atlas compiles with GHC version 9.10.1 or later.
・One is able to utilise Atlas transaction building machinery entirely on client side. If unfortunately, it is deemed not to be possible due to technical challenges, then the reasoning is clearly documented.
ms.report:
Addressing reviewer's feedback: We provide documentation related to compilation of Atlas at https://atlas-app.io/getting-started/how-to-build. To further help with this, we have created a video going over this, please find it here. We further propose to reach out to us either in "Discussion" feature here or via email at hello@geniusyield.co for any further questions and if required, to setup a 1-on-1 session to help with compilation. Also, as noted in the above video, we have a CI in Atlas that compiles it successfully, and can be consulted to see what all was required to be included in build environment for successful compilation. We also updated CI so that it compiles with GHC 9.10.1 (using cabal version 3.14.1.1) — a successful CI run can be seen here. Rest of the submission is same as before.
As part of this milestone, our focus was on following two outputs:
・To make Atlas compile with GHC version 9.10.1 or later.
・Exploration and utilization of Atlas on client side in browsers.

We have made video demonstration, showcasing our achievement of acceptance criteria for these two outputs. Please find it here.
Note that our Atlas framework is fully open-sourced and is accessible here.
Regarding first output, Atlas, now successfully compiles with GHC version 9.10.1 and also with higher version, namely, 9.12.1.
And for second output, unfortunately, after thorough investigation and practical attempts, we have determined that this goal is not feasible due to significant technical difficulties as documented below.
1. Dependency on C Libraries

Atlas relies heavily on IOG/IntersectMBO's Haskell libraries, such as plutus, cardano-ledger, cardano-api. These libraries eventually depend upon cardano-base which includes foundational dependencies such as cardano-crypto-class.
